entities.summary:
Alypius of Alexandria was a Greek writer on music who flourished in the 4th century CE. Born in Alexandria, Egypt, to a wealthy family, Alypius was educated in the traditional Greek schools of Alexandria.

    He became a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of the city, where he engaged in debates and discussions with other notable scholars, including the Christian writer Origen of Alexandria.

    Alypius's most notable work, the "Introduction to Music", survives in a single fragment, which provides valuable insights into the music of the ancient Greeks.

    His contributions to the field of music and his connections to other influential figures of the time make Alypius an important figure in the history of classical music.

    Despite his significance, Alypius's life and works remain somewhat enigmatic, reflecting the limited nature of our knowledge about this obscure figure.
